title: Final graded dataset — LIVE-NOW, ZERO exclusions (operator ruling 2026-10-02, in identical words: there are NO exclusions, NO exceptions; the reference is the live site AS IT IS NOW)
ruling: dataset = the FULL set: every measured page included, zero exclusions. The 26 pages the generation-1 dataset excluded are restored and re-anchored to live-now bytes (anonymous read-only GETs with a browser User-Agent, 2026-10-02). The 4 LIVE-DENIED pages' actual error responses (403/403/403/500) ARE their page expectations. The 15 recorded-disagreement pages' hedged entries are swapped to live-now bytes. Record metadata fields have no live surface (the ?view=record XHR serves 403) and stay frozen — documented here per page.

generation1.note: the exclusion concept is RETIRED as of generation 2; the generation-1 manifest and exclusion manifest survive in git history at these paths (forward commits, never rewrites)

liveNowCapture.method: anonymous read-only GETs, curl + browser User-Agent + shared cookie jar, HTTP/1.1, ~300 ms apart (the proven 247-request-capture discipline)

frozenManifest.note: the CAPTURE photograph; untouched by any overlay generation

interpretationNotes: RECORD FIELDS stay frozen on the restored view-lane lines: the record entry grades engine record metadata vs the seeded corpus; live has no record surface (the classification's ?view=record XHR probes returned 403), and pinning record JSON to denial HTML would compare category-incompatible bytes — instrument corruption, not live truth. The live-now user experience of those pages is carried by their page-lane entries.

mod: tinymce editor's page-lane line changed shape: the generation-1 whole-line CAPTURE_ERROR sentinel (the Ruby oracle's NoMethodError) is replaced by page_html holding live's actual 500 body — the operator's LIVE-DENIED method makes the served error body the expectation. The engine previously pinned byte-identical to the SENTINEL (family-b-verdict lane); grading against live-now re-opens that surface honestly.
HTTP status codes are not part of the byte grading contract (the harness compares render bytes); the live statuses are recorded per swap in this manifest as provenance.

Live-now page bytes carry runtime noise by definition (Cloudflare __CF$cv$params ray ids/timestamps, decko data-slot-id hashes). A port render cannot reproduce those regions; such differences route CONTENT/infra, not engine.
Day-over-day drift check: live-now bytes differ from the 2026-10-02 classification capture in exactly those noise regions (same byte sizes, different shas).
